answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by bonding each identity: every agent locks collateral behind a signed proof-of-personhood root, and rewards flow only through that bond. A small kernel of audited agents issues the roots, while peers in a knoll of trust spot-check for clones reusing the same keys. When twins are found the velvet bond is slashed and the root blacklisted, so an attacker pays a fresh stake per fake and forfeits it on detection, making a large army cost more than it can steal.
